meta.purpose: Comprehensive evidence source for tailoring applications. Intentionally longer than an application resume. Key facts are referenceable claims; strong_points say how far a claim can be pushed for fit, weak_points say what makes it hard to defend. Never paste notes, weak points, or claim checks into an application.
meta.tailoring_rule: Lead with three or four projects most relevant to a role and choose the strongest defensible bullets. Keep role title, dates, model stage, metrics, team contribution, and personally implemented work consistent across the resume and interview.

summaries.text: Machine learning engineer with approximately eight years of experience developing NLP, classical and deep-learning models, and LLM applications. At Thomson Reuters Labs, worked across the ML lifecycle for CLEAR and Checkpoint: secure data and annotation infrastructure, repeatable model training and evaluation, semantic search, production report summarization, and agentic investigation workflows. Designs experiments with researchers and subject-matter experts, translates research code into reusable pipelines, and works with product engineers on delivery in sensitive-data environments.

experience.period_note: September 2026 end date comes from conversation, not an HR record; older resume JSONs say "Present".
experience.notes: Selected work spans multiple products and project phases. Dates are approximate where noted. Confirm official title history.

projects.name: CLEAR entity resolution — retraining and Snowflake pipelines
projects.stage_note: Retraining workflow designed, implemented, and tested; actual adoption not yet documented. Snowflake work is proof of concept. The new XGBoost model was in early testing and used to build a fresh entity database; no production-serving claim.
projects.personal_scope: Designed, proposed, implemented, and tested the SageMaker Pipelines retraining workflow; extended reusable processing components; implemented Snowflake processing and training proofs of concept and assessed migration gaps. Worked specifically on the Snowflake processing pipeline.
projects.team_context: The team trained a new XGBoost entity-matching model to replace a long-running legacy model that was difficult to retrain and had accumulated rule-based workarounds. The team maintained a held-out set, used training and validation splits, addressed the gap between positive-heavy annotations and largely negative candidate pairs, and compared model versions with the legacy system using precision, recall, F1, and SME reviews. Emad recalled roughly eight to ten experimentation rounds and positive SME feedback.
projects.notes: Personal ownership of sampling, feature engineering, and evaluation, along with numerical model results, remains to be pinned down; these are team context, not individual achievement bullets. Worked with model researchers, a lead engineer, and CLEAR product engineering.
bullets: Designed, proposed, implemented, and tested an on-demand retraining workflow using SageMaker Pipelines, bringing researchers' feature-generation, model-training, and metric-calculation code into reusable processing steps.
Enabled researchers to run multiple training experiments in parallel and track experiments through MLflow, reducing manual orchestration and making hypothesis testing more reproducible.
Extended reusable components for SageMaker Python, Poetry-based, and PySpark processing jobs within a DAG-based pipeline repository.
Implemented proof-of-concept Snowflake data-processing and model-training pipelines and assessed compatibility and feature gaps for moving AWS research workflows to Snowflake.
Worked with model researchers, a lead engineer, and CLEAR product engineering to translate research needs into a retraining workflow for the developing entity-resolution system.
